newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BSE storms up in almost record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BSE storms up in almost record turnover.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange joined rising European markets on Wednesday and extended its recent rally as investors breathed a sigh of relief after the U.S. Fed left its interest rates unchanged, traders said.

"Quite a few investors were withholding ahead of yesterday's Fed meeting," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities. "The factor of uncertainty (about interest rate rise) has been eliminated for the time being."
The BUX index closed at 3,899.75 points, up 36.64, ending at a new peak for the fifth successive session.

Traders said the main driving force behind the market's surge was chemicals firm TVK, which continued its record breaking run in brisk trade after newspaper reports that it may receive five billion forints from privatisation agency APV Rt.
"TVK soared as a result of the news about the five billion forints," Agoston said. "But it was also undervalued."
TVK shares closed at 1,830 forints, up 105, but back from a new record high of 1,855 forints reached earlier.
The good sentiment triggered by TVK spilled over to the rest of the market, boosting many shares on the bourse.
"TVK pulled the rest of the shares along," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
"The announcement of the five billion forints left its impact on the market, although it's still uncertain whether they will receive it or not."
Spot share turnover totalled 3.405 billion forints, the highest since the record 5.77 billion reached on August 1, 1995.
Agoston said Richter also contributed to the market's bullish note as market participants were optimistic about the pharmaceuticals stock.
"As for Richter, I explain the rise by expectations of very good results this year and also next year," he said. "The company has huge potential for development."
Richter jumped 120 forints to finish at 9,050.
Elsewhere on the market, the bank stocks ended higher, OTP Bank at 2,720 forints, up 30, and Inter-Europa Bank at 37,000, up 800.
Agoston, in an optimistic mood after the session, said he believed the market was still undervalued.
"I think we are still cheap, we'll still rise," Agoston said, adding he expected foreign funds to give Hungary a bigger allocation of their emerging market portfolio next year.
